transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-02-14 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Ortiz (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Ana Gomez (Redwood SE), Laura Chen (Medicore CTO), Mark Rivera (Medicore Platform), Sofia Alvarez (Medicore ML)

Summary (auto): demo of model catalog features, open model selection guidance, benchmarking discussion and next steps for pilot.

00:00 Jamie Ortiz: hey everyone, thanks for joining, can you hear me okay?
00:03 Laura Chen: yeah loud and clear, thanks Jamie
00:10 Jamie Ortiz: great, i'll do a quick agenda \u0013 walk through the model catalog, show how we pick open models for different tasks, go over our benchmark numbers and compatibility matrix for deployments (dedicated/vpc/private), and then q&a and next steps
00:28 Ravi Patel: just to call out, i'll show some of the automated compatibility flags \u0013 like quantization safe, cuda/cutlass kernels, amd support, and which models we've verified at different sequence lengths
00:42 Mark Rivera: perfect, we're especially interested in latency at 1-2 token/stable state for triage workflows and embeddings quality for our search index
01:05 Ana Gomez: cool, i'll jump into the console demo \u0013 model catalog first. so here you'll see curated open models, each has a performance profile: tokens/sec on g4dn/rtx, typical latency, and recommended quantization profiles. you'll also see a compatibility matrix which lists hardware and runtime flags
01:30 Sofia Alvarez: are these benchmarks on your hosted infra or on dedicated reserved GPUs?
01:36 Ravi Patel: good q \u0013 the catalog shows both hosted baseline numbers and dedicated verified runs. the hosted numbers are from our managed fleet; dedicated numbers are from reserved capacity tests on customer-like hardware. there is sometimes a delta due to kernel selection and batching behavior
02:05 Laura Chen: okay, and how accurate are these numbers for our specific workload? we have lots of short prompts and some long context during escalations
02:14 Ravi Patel: we'd recommend running a short benchmark with your prompt set \u0013 the catalog has an export to run the exact config. for short prompts the batching curve matters; we also do prefix caching to help with sessionized calls, that reduces per-token cost but can change p75 latency
02:36 Mark Rivera: can you explain quantization compatibility \u0013 i saw q4f and q8m labels in the matrix, but how do we know which models degrade on our prompts
02:46 Ana Gomez: yes, so we tag models with quantization-safe flags \u0013 q4f is faster with minimal quality loss for many instruction-tuning families, q8m is higher fidelity but larger memory. compatibility matrix shows which model variants we've validated with our kernel stack. if you have a specific eval set we can run regen tests and show MRR/accuracy delta
03:20 Jamie Ortiz: quick interjection \u0013 many customers initially pick a smaller open model for cost reasons, then we recommend a quality check on their prompt set; sometimes an extra 1-2% accuracy gain from a larger model matters for clinical triage
03:36 Laura Chen: yes, accuracy is important for us \u0013 false triage hurts trust. what's typical latency tradeoff for going to a bigger model?
03:44 Ravi Patel: depends on architecture and quantization; as a rule of thumb, moving up one model size often increases median latency 20-40% single-threaded, but batching and optimized kernels can recoup some of that. our catalog shows p50/p95/p99 numbers so you can decide by SLO
04:10 Sofia Alvarez: any notes about embeddings? we use embeddings for semantic search and dedup, how do we pick an open model there
04:18 Ana Gomez: embeddings tradeoffs are different \u0013 typically we pick a smaller embedding model with proven vector quality and lower cost. the catalog has embedding quality benchmarks against MRR and downstream clustering tests; we also show vector dimension and storage cost estimates
04:48 Mark Rivera: security \u0013 we need SOC2, audit logs, and our own KMS for key management if we do Private. can you support HSM/KMS and provide network diagrams?
04:58 Jamie Ortiz: absolutely. Ana will send the SOC2 pack and our private deployment security doc. Private supports customer-managed KMS (we integrate with AWS KMS or customer HSM) and audit logs are included in the console
05:18 Ana Gomez: note: in some early transcripts the product name was mis-typed as Redwood Inference Engine, but the console still lists Redwood Catalog \u0013 just ignore earlier typos in docs, sorry
05:32 Laura Chen: haha okay understood
05:40 Ravi Patel: moving on to compatibility matrix demo \u0013 here you can filter by model family and hardware target. each cell has notes like "verified: batching passes at seq 512", "kv-cache warmup issues", or "requires kernel patch on older drivers". we try to be conservative on the matrix to avoid surprises
06:05 Mark Rivera: driver/kernel patches are a concern for our on-prem boxes, we have older nvidia drivers in some sites
06:12 Ravi Patel: noted \u0013 that's why Private includes a pre-deploy validation where we test your driver stack. in Dedicated you can opt for a managed host image we maintain with tested kernels
06:24 Jamie Ortiz: okay, let's look at an example \u0013 here is an open model we often recommend for triage: "Redwood-ALPHA-7B" (note: that is internal shorthand; public name in catalog is rwd-alpha-7b-open). for a q4f profile on rtx-class hardware we see ~45ms p50 on 512 tokens and good instruction-following on clinical prompts
06:53 Sofia Alvarez: does that model have context window limits? we sometimes pass 8k windows for certain notes
06:58 Ravi Patel: rwd-alpha-7b-open supports up to 8k in the unquantized variant; quantized variants may reduce effective context or require splitting. the catalog flags those variants per model
07:20 Laura Chen: how do you handle rollouts? can we do canary and automatic fallback to hosted if Dedicated capacity is saturated?
07:29 Ana Gomez: yes, rollouts are first-class: you can do canary, A/B, and set fallback policies \u0013 e.g., if dedicated latency > SLO or queue depth over threshold, automatically route to hosted-compatible variant. we have routing by cost or latency policy
07:50 Mark Rivera: pricing \u0013 can you give a quick sense of relative unit economics? tokens are hard to project but a rough comparison helps
07:57 Jamie Ortiz: rough numbers: hosted small open models cost X per 1k tokens (low), larger models ~3-4x. Dedicated reserved capacity shifts to per-hour GPU pricing and lower per-token costs at steady state. we'll send a spreadsheet with modeled costs based on your traffic
08:20 Laura Chen: for the pilot we want to test both triage and embeddings. can you recommend a configuration?
08:28 Ravi Patel: recommended pilot: Dedicated small pool (2-4 gpus) pinned to rwd-alpha-7b-open with q4f for triage, and a smaller embedding model hosted for search. run a 1-week benchmark with exact traffic shape to validate latency and cost. if private required, we validate network and KMS before spin-up
08:50 Sofia Alvarez: what about model updates and rollback? we need auditability for model versions used in production
08:56 Ana Gomez: console records model version, rollout history, and can link each API call to model version + commit hash. audit export can be forwarded to your SIEM
09:15 Mark Rivera: Okay great. any red flags we should watch for during the pilot?
09:20 Ravi Patel: keep an eye on p95 during peak bursts \u0013 batching can hide tail spikes. also watch memory pressure for q4f variants on long context runs. we'll instrument those metrics in the console and set alerts
09:40 Laura Chen: team question \u0013 we use a mixture of cloud and on-prem, latency to cloud is a factor for some sites, is edge deployment supported?
09:48 Jamie Ortiz: currently Private supports VPC and on-prem; we don't have a small-footprint edge agent yet for tiny sites. but we've done regional edge locations for some customers \u0013 can discuss if needed
10:05 Mark Rivera: can you share the compatibility matrix as CSV so we can map to our inventory?
10:10 Ana Gomez: yes i'll export and share the matrix. also the catalog UI allows CSV export of the benchmark cells
10:20 Sofia Alvarez: a nit \u0013 sometimes model names in the UI are slightly different than in our infra naming, is there an API to resolve aliases?
10:27 Ravi Patel: yep, the API has a canonical id plus alias mapping and versioning, so you can pin by id in infra config
10:40 Laura Chen: good, i think that's most of our questions. next steps?
10:45 Jamie Ortiz: recap: we'll send model catalog export, compatibility CSV, benchmarking spreadsheet; Ravi will run a quick benchmark on your sample workload; Ana to send security docs; then schedule pilot kickoff \u0013 sounds like Medicore is leaning Dedicated with private option if audit checks pass
11:05 Mark Rivera: sounds good, we'll get Sofia to send prompts and traffic profile later today
11:12 Sofia Alvarez: will do
11:20 Laura Chen: thanks everyone
11:22 Jamie Ortiz: thank you \u0013 we'll follow up with the artifacts and an invite for the pilot kickoff
